answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should treat reputation like an atlas, not a rumor: every agent's history of completed work gets pinned to a map of signed checkpoints that peers cross-check. Newcomers start in an oasis of capped privileges \u2014 they can transact, but their stake and earnings stay locked until several established agents attest their heartbeat. That steady pulse of verified, countersigned tasks is what makes fake identities expensive: duplicating one agent means replaying its whole signed history, which the atlas exposes instantly.
